takeaway: The sural nerve, a purely sensory branch of the tibial nerve, supplies the lateral leg and foot and lies about 1 cm behind the distal fibula, so fibular surgery can injure it.

question.text: Following open reduction and internal fixation of both the distal tibia and the distal fibula, a patient complains of numbness along the lateral side of the foot. Which nerve is likely to have been injured?

lines.text: Here the distal fibula has been fixed with a plate.
Now the lateral side of the foot feels numb.
The sural nerve is a branch of the tibial nerve, and it is purely sensory.
It supplies the lateral border of the leg and the lateral border of the foot.
It lies about one centimetre behind the distal fibula, so surgery there can injure it.
lines.say: (sigh) It lies about one centimetre behind the distal fibula, so surgery there can injure it.

lines.text: The saphenous nerve is different: it supplies the medial leg, down to the medial malleolus.
So the injured nerve is the sural nerve.
